Adding some technical detail for the lab plan so Joe’s team knows what we’ll measure and how we’ll configure the engine: 

Test harness notes:
- We’ll provide a Dockerized harness that can be run inside your VPC to generate identical request patterns for both Redwood and hyperscaler endpoints. Harness includes: request distribution generator, token counter, latency histograms, and a small agent that tags each request with a run-id.
- Model variants: we’ll test two variants: rwd-7b-fp16 and rwd-7b-int8 (quant). If you want the 13B we can add but it increases compute and cost.
- Batching strategy: dynamic batching with a target batch size of 32 and a max-batch-wait of 12ms for the sustained runs; for the burst test we’ll allow larger batches up to 64 to emulate queued microbursts.
- KV cache / prefix caching: we’ll run both warm and cold cache profiles. Warm cache expected to improve tokens/sec by ~18-28% depending on request overlap.

Measurement specifics (how we compute p95/p99):
- Server-side latency per request recorded at the runtime (time of request arrival -> time of last token output). For hyperscalers, we’ll run the same agent and capture remote-server timestamps, then derive comparable latency excluding external internet noise (we’ll peer in the same region).
- Tokens/sec: measured as total tokens returned divided by effective generation time (exclude input/serialization overhead). We’ll report rolling tokens/sec, median window, and 95th/99th windows.

Preliminary performance expectation (rough from our internal microbenchmarks):
- rwd-7b-fp16: 1.8k–2.2k tokens/sec per GPU under steady-state for 250-token median requests (p95 latency ~140–250ms depending on batching and sequence length).
- rwd-7b-int8: +30–40% throughput gain (roughly 2.4k–3.0k tokens/sec), p95 improved 20–35ms in many cases.

Notes / asks for Stratify:
- Please confirm target region and whether you want hyperscaler runs in us-west-2 or us-east-1. Network locality matters for raw p95 numbers.
- Provide a single representative API key for the hyperscaler endpoints if you want us to orchestrate their runs (otherwise we’ll give the harness and you run them).

I’ll attach the initial harness config and a CSV template for the payload distribution.
